verdict.rationale: Jules documents that a submitted task, entered directly or by labeling a GitHub issue with "jules", is turned into a generated plan that the developer reviews and approves before any code changes. That is the core of the intent-to-spec flow. However, the docs never state that input is free-form plain language, and they do not describe how the plan scopes or breaks down the work. Community reports also note quality falls off beyond simple problems. missing for 10: explicit documentation that plain-language feature or bug descriptions are accepted, detail on how the generated plan scopes the task (files, steps, acceptance criteria), independent hands-on corroboration of plan quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can describe a feature or bug in plain language and have it automatically turned into a scoped implementation task

citations.quote: Once you submit a task, Jules will generate a plan. You can review and approve it before any code changes are made.
